summary:
Role D (harness and docs) is done. Harness milestone d5-sandbox-bitwise is written. Docs are updated for B: the README dialect section, NOTICE, roadmap rows 146, 147, 196 and 206, a new [x] round-3 row and four follow-up rows, and the LuaJITStateFactory.java comment. OcljArch.scala is unchanged.

The d5 expected line comes from PUC 5.3.6, not from me: ok/1:0/-2147483648:0/inexact>>/inexact|/0:0/0:1/noint/0:16/11:98566144/2097151:4294967295/0:16777215. I extracted the probe exactly as it sits in OcljSmoke.scala (md5 bfd57f4e6b6a) and ran it standalone [M]:
- The B reference equals that line with JIT on, with -joff, and with -O3 -Ohotloop=1.
- PUC 5.3.6 with the B rule applied to each operator equals it, on Windows and on Linux (identical once CRLF is stripped).
- Today's b0 fails. Its output equals the bw32 line, so the milestone reports the 32-bit message.
- The round-3 A prototype (rounding instead of raising) fails at rows 3 and 4 only.

The Scala compiles: I repeated smoke-test.sh's compile step (javac, then scalac 2.13.11 on JDK 17) into fresh scratch dirs. It exits 0 with the same 26 classes and the same 5 deprecation warnings as HEAD. A one-line sabotage makes it fail. Nothing was run in the harness.

Every example in the README and the new roadmap text was checked on bB against PUC 5.3.6 (README examples all in one script; NaN/inf, which negative n raise, the scanner residual, hex-float rounding and Color.lua in separate small checks). Where the shipped build's figure is needed, the text says TODO-MEASURE: 3 places in README, 10 in the roadmap.

checks: [M] Probe extracted from OcljSmoke.scala lines 3805-3862, margins stripped, a print appended (md5 bfd57f4e6b6a; re-extracted after the last edit, same md5). Run as-is on bB (jit on), bB -joff and bB -O3 -Ohotloop=1: all three print the expected line.

[M] FAIL-FIRST: today's b0 luajit.exe (md5 2e737b868794), jit on and -joff, prints ok/0:1/-1:2147483648/0:2147483647/0:1073741825/0:1/0:1/0:0/E/0:0/0:2097151/0:16777215. That is 9 of 11 fields wrong, and it equals the milestone's bw32 literal. Second fail-first: the A prototype synth/b1 (md5 0cd8b30da700) prints 2147483648:0 and 1073741824:0 at rows 3 and 4 (rounded, not raised), so d5 FAILs there too.

[M] PUC side: twin-puc-B.lua wraps every operator in the B rule (math.tointeger(r + 0.0) == r, else the error). Windows PUC 5.3.6 and Linux PUC 5.3.6 both print exactly the expected line (CR-stripped md5 249f83746f14, the same as bB's output). I took the Scala bwWant and bw32 literals out of the source with grep/sed and compared mechanically: bB jon/joff and both PUC twins PASS; b0 jon/joff, b1 jon/joff and raw PUC (no rule) FAIL.

[M] Provenance step 2 (raw-puc-int.lua: PUC 5.3.6 with no rule, %d output, significant bits counted with integer ops only). Rows 3 and 4 have 63 significant bits; every other row has 53 or fewer (row 10 has exactly 53, row 7 raises noint). So the twin raises exactly where the raw integer is over 53 bits.
[M] The hot loop compiles: LUA_PATH set to each tree's src, then -jv shows [TRACE 1 bitprobe:20 loop] on both bB and b0, with no abort.

[M] Compile check (compile-harness.sh: smoke-test.sh step 2 into a fresh dir, javac + scalac 2.13.11 on JDK 17; nothing is run). HEAD copy: scalac exit 0, 26 classes, 5 deprecations. Edited file: exit 0, 26 classes, 5 deprecations, and Smoke$.class contains 'OCLJBIT=' (HEAD's has 0). FAIL-FIRST: sab1 copy with bwNames(i) changed to bwNamez(i) gives scalac exit 1, 'OcljSmoke.scala:5844: error: not found: value bwNamez'.

[M] README/roadmap claims (readme-claims.lua on bB and PUC 5.3.6): 1<<32, 1<<63, -1>>63, 1<<64, 8<<-1, -1>>1 raises, (n>>8)&0xFF raises for n=-2 while the masked form gives 255 = PUC, ~0>>1 raises, ~0>>11 = 2^53-1, '3'&1 = 1, '0x10'|0 = 16, '0xffffffffffffffff'|0 = -1, '1.5'|0, 1.5&1 and 2^63|0 raise noint, -2^63|0 computes, nil&1 and local t&1 messages in LuaJIT word order versus PUC's, tostring(1<<47) = 1.4073748835533e+14 with %d exact, 0x00ff00ff00ff00ff&0xff = 0 vs 255, the three big literals raise vs PUC's -1/maxinteger/mininteger, x <<= 40 = 2^40, -8 ~>> 1 = -4, -1 ~>> 64 = -1. naninf.lua: NaN, inf and -inf raise noint, the same as PUC. Not every negative n raises: -2 and -256 raise, -2^62 and -2^63 compute (README wording narrowed to 'most negative n').

[M] The README statement 'every operator is exact for operands non-negative and below 2^32, any shift count': u32claim.lua ran 1,704,000 operations with 0 raised, jit on and -joff. FAIL-FIRST: the same script with -2 among the operands gives 800 raised.
[M] Scanner residual (resid.lua): '1e-1048576'|0 and '1e1048576'|0 give the type error on bB; PUC gives 0 and noint (Windows and Linux alike).
[M] Hex-float instrument note (hexf1.lua): '0x1.0000000000000801p52'|0 and tonumber of it give 4503599627370496 on Windows PUC; Linux PUC and bB give 4503599627370497.
[M] MineOS Color.lua 5.3 chunk (file lines 13-62, from the census copy): bB and b0 both report 'lua53colorfunctions:16: unexpected symbol near '/''; PUC 5.3.6 loads it.
[M] Line endings: CR count 0 (tr -cd '\r' | wc -c) in all five repo files and all scratch scripts.

[I] The stock arm paints 'absent'. Not run: there is no PUC 5.2 interpreter here. Reasoning: the operators sit only inside load()'s string, 5.2's lexer has no << token, so load returns nil; everything outside load() is plain 5.2 Lua.
deviations: Probe restructured, as B requires. Under B, rows 3 and 4 (~0>>1, (1<<62)|1) raise, so the design's single pcall would have turned the whole row into 'error/...'. Each row now runs in its own pcall through a classifier X: 'inexact<op>' for the B message (so the operator is checked too), 'noint', or 'E'. Row 7 now shows 'noint' instead of the old '1.5ok'/'noint' pair; b0's row 8 shows 'E' instead of 'strE'.

Two rows added beyond the design's nine. ~0 >> 11 (2^53-1, the widest exact result) shows B's boundary. (n & 0xFFFFFFFF) >> 8 for n = -2 is the README's remedy. The remedy row gives the same value on b0, so it has no fail-first power of its own; the line as a whole does. The expected line was derived from PUC with the rule applied, not written by hand.

OCLJBIT has its own screen row (39) instead of being appended to row 16 like d4. Row 16 holds about 100 of the 160 columns and OCLJBIT is about 110 more. Row 39 is free: suite rows are 24-32 with all 9 references, gc rows 37/38, encore 41. It is painted every tick like row 16, so the paint timer makes one more direct gpu.set per tick (12 instead of 11).
OcljArch.scala is unchanged. Its comment lists only library contents (string.pack in STRING); round 3 adds no library feature and no token there.
The milestone also carries a field-by-field diff and a specific message for today's 32-bit line (bw32, measured on the round-2 build). d4 has neither.

Roadmap 'row 206: the 32-bit sentence is resolved': that 32-bit sentence is actually in row 146 (its Status 2026-10-16). I marked it resolved in row 146's new status. Row 206 (the FFI row) got the ±2^51 JIT/interpreter finding as 'Found 2026-10-17, fixed by round 3', which points back to row 146.

Follow-up rows: CRC32, metamethods + // + __idiv, and F17 are separate rows, in that order after the round-3 row. The three smaller items (u8/u16 width, RESID-scan, loop-invariant shift-count abort) and the Windows-PUC instrument note are numbered (1)-(4) in one 'smaller follow-ups' row, in the style of the roadmap's existing 'loose ends' rows.
No fix1 timing in the roadmap. design-B's 0.023 s is for A+fix1, not for 'without fix1', so it cannot show fix1's effect. Only the qualitative effect (blacklisted, now compiles) is stated.
The new [x] row's title says 'built TODO-MEASURE'. Its speed and GG figures are labelled as the prototype's, each with a 'shipped: TODO-MEASURE'.
open_questions: Harness fail-first and pass runs are main-session work. With the round-2 native the additive arm must FAIL d5 with '<- LuaJIT's 32-bit BitOp results'. Stock must show 'absent' (unmeasured here). After the build, every arm wants the expected line. Each arm's check count goes up by one.

The README and roadmap name C1/C2/C3 files: test/native/run-bitop.sh, run-bitfuzz.sh, run-bitjit.sh, negctl-bitop.sh, test/native/bitop/deviations.txt, bitop_test.c, the E:INEXACT kind and coerce_agree. If a role names them differently, those references need updating.

Row 196 says build-native.sh stage 4 observes tonumber("1") << 32 on luajit.exe (design §4). Role A's build-native.sh had no bitop blocks yet when I checked, so confirm the gate exists as described. The roadmap deliberately does not name the luajit.exe gate file (design calls it bitops.lua).

TODO-MEASURE to fill in. README: check count, failures and date in the smoke-suite row. Roadmap: the round-3 row's build date; shipped speed; for-in fixture bytes; GG_State; run-bitop's three case counts; run-bitfuzz's campaign; negctl-bitop's arm count; row 196's new serializer hash.
Row 147's 'nothing in Color.lua's 5.3 chunk would raise the 53-bit error once // parses' comes from reading the code (24-bit non-negative colours), not from a run.

The extra per-tick gpu.set for row 39 is negligible by my reading but unmeasured. If the main session prefers zero added calls, OCLJBIT could go on short row 15 or 20 instead; neither layout has been run in the harness.
